text.c1_title: Until 2019 the Nifty rose on a rising P/E. Since then, earnings have done the lifting.
text.c1_sub1: Over ten years the Nifty rose 2.6 times and its earnings 2.7 to 2.8 times (like-for-like), so its P/E ends a little below where it started.
text.c1_sub2: NSE switched from standalone to consolidated earnings on 31 Mar 2021, which cut its P/E from 40.4x to 33.2x overnight. Lighter lines show the old basis.
text.c1_foot1: Source: NSE Indices (Nifty 50 P/E, trailing four quarters, month-end; via Downstox, checked against NSE Index Dashboards), Yahoo Finance (Nifty 50 daily closes). Earnings per unit = Nifty close ÷ NSE P/E. Data to 28 Sep 2026.
text.c1_foot2: Like-for-like: pre-2021 standalone earnings restated to a consolidated basis with a ratio of 1.14 (Bloomberg 10-year average) to 1.205 (NSE's switch day). Motilal Oswal's tally of actual Nifty EPS rose from ₹393 (FY16) to ₹1,065 (FY26), 2.7x.

method_lines: How this workbook was built

1. Nifty 50 daily closes, 1 Sep 2016 to 28 Sep 2026, come from Yahoo Finance (^NSEI, NSE data). Every year was transcribed twice by independent agents and the two copies were diffed; all rows matched, and every month-end close matches Yahoo's monthly table. One missing day (29 Mar 2019) was filled from Yahoo's monthly table.

2. NSE's Nifty 50 P/E (index market cap divided by trailing four-quarter earnings, as NSE Indices publishes it daily) is taken at each month-end from Downstox, which republishes NSE's series. 26 of these values were checked against NSE's own monthly Index Dashboards and Nippon India MF's daily notes; the largest gap was 0.08, which is Downstox's one-decimal rounding. September 2026 uses the 28 Sep 2026 reading (19.26).
3. Earnings per unit = Nifty close / NSE P/E. This is NSE's trailing earnings for the index, as NSE counts them.

4. On 31 Mar 2021 NSE switched from standalone to consolidated earnings. The P/E fell from 40.43 to 33.20 overnight while the index moved about 1%, so consolidated earnings were about 20.5% higher than standalone that day (Summary!B9).

5. Like-for-like columns multiply pre-2021 earnings by a ratio (Summary!B11) to put them on a consolidated basis. The ratio was not constant: Bloomberg data put the 10-year average at 1.14 and Dec 2020 at 1.16, against 1.205 at NSE's switch. The Summary shows results at both ends of that range.
6. Motilal Oswal's bottom-up tally of actual Nifty EPS (FY16 ₹393 to FY26 ₹1,065, 2.7x) is shown on the Validation sheet as an independent check.
What the numbers are, and what they are not

NSE's P/E is a trailing measure: it divides today's price by the last four quarters of reported profit. It is not the forward (expected-earnings) P/E that Bloomberg charts use, so its levels are higher; on 28 Sep 2026 NSE showed 19.3x while Bloomberg's forward P/E was about 17x.

Long-run "average Nifty P/E" figures quoted in the press (23x to 27x over 10 years) mostly mix the standalone and consolidated eras, so they overstate the average on today's basis. The consolidated-era median here is about 22x.
The Nifty figures are the price index, without dividends. The total-return index grew about 1.3 percentage points a year faster over the ten years to July 2026 (NSE via Bajaj Finserv AMC).
